subject: POC wiring sprint — ownership roster & action windows
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@carebridge.com>
Cc: Jared Lopez <jared.lopez@cloudcorp.net>
Date: 2026-06-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC wiring sprint — kickoff intentions and quick asks

Hi all,

Thanks for the time yesterday — looping up a short kickoff note so we have a common set of owners for the POC wiring sprint. Goal: get a lab-like POC environment standing with API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, and VPC peering in a 2-week window.

High level asks to start (please flag if anything is off):
- CareBridge: confirm preferred peering CIDRs and the desired CIDR block we should target for peering.
- CareBridge: confirm whether you want customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed (we support both).
- Redwood (ops): allocate a sandbox org and ephemeral API key set (read-only and test-write).
- Security: provide the SOC2 evidence link and a brief note on acceptable logging retention for the POC.

I'm attaching a first draft MAP (RDI_CareBridge_MAP_v0.3.xlsx) and a simple wiring roster CSV that lists who will own each step. Marcus and Mina will cover Redwood network steps; Evelyn will own API key provisioning and audit hooks on our side. Alex / Ops on your side, please complete the rightmost columns in the roster with ETA.

Proposed immediate cadence:
- This week: agree CIDRs, KMS choice, and API key model.
- Next week: schedule peering maintenance window and exchange peering test routes.

Next step: Alex, can you confirm the CIDR and whether you want us to initiate a Cloud Router / Transit Gateway connection or if you'll request the peering on your side?

Thanks,
Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@carebridge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@carebridge.com>
Date: 2026-06-07T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC wiring sprint — kickoff intentions and quick asks

Thanks Marcus — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) CIDR: we can open 10.40.0.0/16 for the POC peering. Will carve smaller /24s on our side for each test cluster (we'll list them in the roster).
2) KMS: we prefer customer-managed KMS (Azure Key Vault). We'll need a short doc from you about the recommended key rotation policy for the POC (30 vs 90 days).
3) API keys: we want an ephemeral key for the eval team and a longer-lived key for automated ingestion (scoped to embeddings endpoint). We also need the token format so our infra can add it to Secret Store.

Can you also provide any constraints on source IPs for callbacks? We'll put the ops@carebridge team on the roster for peering firewall changes.

If you can drop the MAP into a shared Drive link we can update the timeline columns.

Alex

Hey Alex,

Appreciate the quick replies. A couple of concrete items from Redwood ops/security side to keep the POC lean and audit-friendly: 

1) API key model: we will create two key classes for the POC — EPHEMERAL (30d auto-rotate) and SERVICE (90d, limited to embeddings & generate). Keys are scoped by route and we provide a JWK thumbprint if you want to pin in your secret manager.

2) Org setup: I will create a sandbox org named cb-poc-2026 and add CareBridge read-only SSO users. For initial testing we'll add the eval users you listed; prod-facing service accounts can be created later.

3) IP allowlist: for callbacks and webhooks please allow these Redwood egress ranges for the POC: 34.83.12.0/24, 34.83.13.0/24. If you'd prefer narrower single-IP ranges we can negotiate specific NAT IPs.

4) VPC peering approach: Redwood can initiate a cloud-to-cloud peering (we'll open the Cloud Router config). If you prefer to request peering on your side we can provide the peering template (attached: poc_network_template.yaml) for your network team.

5) Logging & retention: for the POC we keep 30 days of request logs by default; if you need extended retention we can route to your S3/Azure blob for the period you specify.

I've attached a lightweight wiring ownership roster (wiring_ownership_roster.csv) and a simple network diagram. Marcus/Evelyn: assigning API-key creation and JWK delivery to Evelyn — can you confirm ETA?

Action items for next 48 hours:
- Alex / CareBridge: confirm 10.40.0.0/16 acceptance and whether you'll request peering or have us initiate.
- CareBridge: confirm KMS choice (you noted Azure Key Vault) and share access method.
- Evelyn: create ephemeral/service keys and share JWK thumbprints in the Drive link.

Thanks,
Mina

- I created the EPHEMERAL key and SERVICE key in our sandbox org (cb-poc-2026). EPHEMERAL key id: rk-ephem-6f2d; SERVICE key id: rk-svc-23b9.

- ETA for handing off the production-like service account: EOD Thu (2026-06-10) once we finish the access review.

Great — thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. Confirming acceptance of the Redwood egress ranges for callbacks and 10.40.0.0/16 for peering. We will request the peering on our side and start the firewall change window Friday 6/11 02:00–04:00 UTC (Ops prefers off-hours).

Jared: can you confirm transit configuration and whether any ASN changes are needed?

I'll update the Drive MAP and mark the handwritten ETA for the peering request. If all goes well we'll move to an initial run on Monday 6/14.

Short note: we also need a one-hour handoff on Monday morning to run through the API keys and test embeddings ingestion. Can Redwood propose a 9–10am PT slot?

Appreciate the team sprint — Alex
